comment: No source is published; read from the maker's manual. Inputs A and B and outputs A and B get no family: the module copies whatever is patched into them. THE PASS-THROUGH SWITCHES ARE REVERSED in this build. A gate byte is what output 1, named Gate Open, is set to 10V from. Output 3 (Output A) is written from input 2 only when that byte is zero, and output 4 (Output B) only when it is non-zero. The maker's port descriptions read 'Passes Input A when Gate is Open' and 'Passes Input A when Gate is Low' (the second is also a typo for Input B), and the manual says the same. The panel groups Gate Open with the A row and Gate Low with the B row, so a person reading the panel will get it wrong too. The Mode switch prints an infinity sign for repeat and a 1 for one shot; a value of 1 is repeat.
